 Metals Gold falls more than 2% as CPI tops forecasts, lifting dollar and yields
 Published Tue, Nov 10 2026 12:46 AM EST Updated 2 Hours Ago WATCH LIVE In this article
 @GC26Z 
 Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Gold prices eased on Tuesday as investors took profits after bullion's more than 1% rally in the previous session, while awaiting U.S. inflation data for clues on the Federal Reserve's policy path. Brendon Thorne | Bloomberg | Getty Images Gold prices fell more ​than 2% on Tuesday ​after hotter-than-expected U.S. ​inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields while reinforcing expectations of a bigger interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve this year.
 Spot gold was down 2.1% ⁠at $4,051.50 ‌an ounce, while U.S. ⁠gold futures for December delivery fell 1.3% to $4,059.30 an ounce.
 "Both the overall number CPI and the core CPI came in a shade above estimates. All in all, it wasn't as ‌great as the markets were hoping for," said Edward Meir, an analyst at Marex.
 The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% last month ​after advancing 0.6% in September, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a 0.3% month-on-month rise.
 Bets on a 50-basis point Fed rate hike in December started to build ⁠after the inflation print and comments by Fed governor Christopher Waller saying he would ‌support more aggressive action in the event of a ‌too-hot Consumer Price Index report.
 The probability of a 25 bp cut is fully priced in, while the possibility of a 50 bp hike rose to around 13.6%, ⁠from 0% before the data, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
 The U.S. dollar ⁠index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six other ⁠major currencies, rose and Treasury yields climbed.
 A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for holders of other currencies, while higher Treasury ​yields increase the opportunity cost of holding ‌non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.
 The Monetary Authority of Singapore said on Tuesday it would launch a vaulting service to hold bullion for foreign central banks and lower taxes on some companies in the gold market as it competes for a ​bigger slice of the precious metals ‌trade.
 Spot silver fell 2.9% to $51.86 per ounce and palladium was down 1.0% at $1,031.20.
